newsitem.title: USA: Staples president confident of FTC approval.
newsitem.headline: Staples president confident of FTC approval.

text.p: Staples Inc president Martin Hananka said Tuesday he is confident that the U.S. Federal Trade Commission will approve the company's plan to sell 63 stores to OfficeMax Inc and then merge with Office Depot Inc.

"I think the (FTC) staff has felt that this would be a potential fix to their concern and we're optimistic that we'll be getting the green light over the next couple of weeks," he told reporters following a luncheon speech in Boston.
Hananka said Staples officials talked over the weekend with OfficeMax and would soon finalize the sale announced earlier this month of 63 Staples and Office Depot stores for $108.75 million.
"The divestiture plan is about to the signed," he said. "Our people worked over the weekend and we're optimistic that our divestiture plan is acceptable with the FTC."

He said the terms of the deal with OfficeMax have not changed. He added that he is unaware of any additional requests from the FTC for information or if the company has had any talks in recent days with the commission.

The FTC voted against the proposed $4 billion merger on March 10, saying it would raise prices for consumers. Staples amended the deal by agreeing to the sale of 63 stores to rival OfficeMax on March 12.
FTC Chairman Robert Pitofsky has said that prices for business supplies and accessories are higher in those cities which have fewer office supply superstores.

However, Hananka said the merger would result in synergies which would enable Staples to cut costs and pass the savings to customers. "We're in it to lower prices and we're going to pass through lower prices to the customer," he said.

The merged company would open 150 stores this year and 200 stores over the next two years in North America, Hananka said. More than 1,000 stores would be remodelled following the merger and about a "handful" of existing stores would be closed, he said.
Hananka said the merger would create an office superstore powerhouse with more than $12 billion in revenues annually and more than 1,100 stores in every major market in North America.
It would also merge the companies' fledgling operations in Europe, which would serve as a platform for future growth, he said.
"It's a few years away where we say we are ready to go out and build hundreds of stores in Europe," he said. "There's enough growth in this business in North America to last a long time."
